instruction: Extract all the slide titles from my LibreOffice Impress presentation 'Dickinson_Slides.pptx' and save them in a Word document called 'slide_titles.docx' on the Desktop. Each title should be on its own line in the document.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting all slide titles from the PowerPoint presentation and saving them to a Word document. Verified by reading the actual PowerPoint file: 9 slides with titles listed in expected_titles. The evaluator reads the Word document and checks if all 9 titles match (case-insensitive).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: Word document creation at correct path, all 9 slide titles extracted, correct number and content of titles
Getter logic is correct: extracts paragraph texts from Word document, filters empty lines, returns list of title strings

Metric logic is correct: properly handles expected parameter (accesses 'expected_titles' directly since get_rule returns rules dict), compares count and content with case-insensitive and whitespace-normalized matching
Coverage is complete: checks file existence (implicit via env.controller.get_file), title count (9), and exact title content match
Semantic verification is appropriate: evaluates the output (Word document contents) rather than the process, which is standard for verification tasks
